_note: FIRST baseline for this profile. 075 recorded it in-file only, so Article VIII §2's ±5% budget had nothing to compare against; 082 T046 (FR-022(a) / SC-012 / K10) creates it. Release build, --benchmark_min_time=0.5s, 4 runs. READ THE per-benchmark spread fields before treating any single figure as a gate: this profile's run-to-run spread is 9-18%, so a ±5% budget is NOT resolvable on one run and must be evaluated against `measured_release_us_runs`.
_before_side_caveat: FIX44 / FIX50SP2 ONLY: the pre-change (T002) figures for those two rows are n=1 — a single run captured before implementation, with no spread recorded. Their variance is therefore unbounded and the before/after deltas MUST NOT be read as precise. What the data does support is the weaker, sufficient claim: no regression. The FIX44 / FIX50SP2 deltas are NEGATIVE (faster) by 34-44%, which is outside this profile's measured 9-18% run-to-run spread in the same direction, so Article VIII §2's no-regression obligation is met without needing the exact magnitude to be trustworthy. The speed-up itself is NOT root-caused and is deliberately not claimed as a 082 improvement. FIX42 is DIFFERENT and does not carry this caveat: its pre-change figure was measured n=4, back-to-back with the post-change figure at Gate B round 1 (see that row's `_pre_change_provenance`), so its ±spread is bounded exactly as the post-change side's is.

benchmarks.name: BM_TableView_BuildFix42
benchmarks.verdict: MEASURED, LARGE POSITIVE DELTA (+44.9% median) — Article VIII §2 INTENTIONAL perf change per FR-022's own opening declaration, not a regression to be explained away. FIX 4.2 registered ZERO repeating groups pre-082 (L-063-1); 082 makes group detection structural, so it now registers 18 groups and this row measures work that did not previously exist. The number bounds the added cost; it is not a pass/fail gate.
benchmarks._pre_change_provenance: Gate B round 1 (PR #261 review, fixpp#261, 2026-08-13) — MEASURED RETROACTIVELY, NOT captured at T002/T046 as FR-022(a) asked. A throwaway git worktree at `main` (c8eb4fec) had BM_TableView_BuildFix42 back-ported VERBATIM from this branch's bench/dictionary/table_view_footprint_bench.cpp (the row loads FIX42.xml outside the timed loop and times only as_table_view() — no 082-only API), configured with the same linux-clang-release Conan profile (via `conan install` + `cmake -B`, since `cmake --preset` cannot be used in a fresh worktree — Conan's CMakeUserPresets.json preset-name collision), and built. Both sides were then run --benchmark_min_time=0.5s, 4 runs each, BACK-TO-BACK on this same host under the same load (load average 0.6-1.05 across both legs, within the same ~15-second window) — the only comparison T049 found valid on this machine, since a cross-session magnitude comparison is provably uninterpretable here (vt11, which 082 does not touch, moved -35% between two measurement sessions with zero code change). This retroactive figure replaces the false claim this row originally shipped with ('NEW ROW — no pre-change counterpart EXISTS'): a pre-change figure WAS obtainable at T002/T046 via this exact back-port-and-measure technique (the technique the branch itself later used for T049's 8-profile A/B), and remains obtainable now. Filling in a number while implying it was captured pre-implementation would replace a false rationale with a false provenance — hence this field.
benchmarks._post_change_remeasurement_note: `measured_release_us_runs` above ([487,477,491,481], median 484) is a FRESH 2026-08-13 head-side batch, re-measured (not the 2026-08-12 batch originally checked into this row: [455,466,466,426], median 460) SPECIFICALLY so the head-side figure is back-to-back with the pre-change worktree run in the same load window (see `_pre_change_provenance`'s ~15-second window for that pairing) — cross-session pairing is exactly what `_before_side_caveat` and T049 (implementation-notes.md) warn is invalid here. `context.date` (2026-08-12) still describes the original FIX44/FIX50SP2 measurement session; this row's own figures are 2026-08-13. An earlier draft of this note (predating Gate B round 2) described the gap between the 2026-08-12 and 2026-08-13 batches as '~7 seconds apart'; that is wrong, since the two batches were captured on different calendar dates, not seconds apart — the exact interval between them was not recorded, so none is stated here. That same earlier draft also mislabeled '~7.9%' as the 'min-to-min' drift between the two batches: the TRUE min-to-min (426 -> 477) is +11.97%, and 7.9% is actually 455 -> 491 (the old batch's first run to the fresh batch's max) — neither a min nor a median comparison. Between-batch drift on the SAME binary is therefore restated per basis: median-to-median (460 -> 484) is +5.10%, consistent with this profile's own documented 9-18% run-to-run spread (see the top-level `_note`) and well inside it; the harsher true min-to-min (426 -> 477) is +11.97%. Against those two bases, +44.9% is 8.8x the median-to-median drift and 3.7x the true min-to-min drift. The delta therefore clears observed between-batch drift on every basis, but the earlier claim that it 'clears that drift by >5x' held only on the median and on the mislabeled 7.9% figure, not on the true min-to-min, and is retracted as stated. Median-to-median is the right primary basis, since it is what this row's own `measured_release_us_median` reports — the paired measurement and the +44.9% delta both stand.
benchmarks._group_bits_note: The heap half of FR-022(a). sizeof(table_view) is unchanged (row 1), but `group_bits_` is a std::vector<std::uint64_t> that goes EMPTY -> (max registered no_tag >> 6) + 1 words per table_view COPY on FIX40/41/42. Measured 7 words = 56 B for FIX 4.2, vs 0 words pre-082 (FIX 4.2 registered zero groups then — a valid before/after, not a broken counter). Derived in-bench from the public group_first_field() accessor, not from the private member, so the figure is reproducible.

_predicted_cost_not_observed: T046's task text predicted a slowdown on EVERY dictionary — including the byte-identical ones — because the per-field group test goes from one enum compare to an O(log G) binary search over `groups_` (G = 507 on FIX50SP2, ~9 comparisons). That cost is NOT observable at this profile's granularity: FIX50SP2 and FIX44 both measured faster than the n=1 pre-change figure. Recorded as measured rather than as predicted, per Article VIII's 'asserting any leg unmoved instead of measuring it is non-conforming'.
